reason: I want to see what the kidney filter lets through before following the recovery route.
expectation: I expect small substances, including useful ones, to pass through while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would help connect the urinary organs, but I want to follow filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose, salts and water through along with wastes, so I want to follow their recovery.
reaction: It was interesting that filtering doesn't just remove waste.
reason: The recovery tube is shown taking useful substances back toward the blood.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, leaving fluid with wastes behind.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to see recovery first.

effect: Useful substances and much water return to blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to continue down the tube. I can now build its route out.
reaction: It makes more sense why recovery matters after filtering.
reason: The ureters connect the kidneys toward the bladder, so I'll start the drainage route there.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidneys, leaving the bladder to connect afterward.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the bladder first, but following the route from the kidneys seems clearer.

effect: The ureters are fitted, so the bladder is the remaining connection for the urinary organs.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the bladder provides a place for urine to collect.
expectation: I expect the bladder to connect to the ureters, completing the basic drainage route.

effect: The bladder is fitted, completing the route from the kidneys through the ureters to urine storage.
reaction: The explanation makes the ureters' role clear.
reason: I'll follow the recovered kidney fluid into the completed urinary route first.
expectation: I expect the remaining waste-containing fluid to become urine and travel toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the organs to the body also advances a goal, but I want to finish following the fluid first.

effect: The remaining fluid follows the urinary route as urine, while blood continues separately; the filtering goal is complete.
reaction: Seeing the two routes stay separate makes the process clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect the urinary organs to the body.
expectation: I expect the kidneys, ureters and bladder to be added to the body model, completing the remaining goal.

effect: The urinary organs are now connected to the body's circulation, completing the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the whole route connected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the filtered fluid through recovery was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidneys take useful substances and water back into the blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was straightforward and less interesting on its own, though it completed the route.

surprise.text: I was surprised that useful glucose and water pass through the filter along with waste rather than the filter picking out only waste.

arbitrary.text: None felt especially arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained the parts' purposes, even when there was only one combination offered.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter because following the kidney fluid made a familiar organ's job clearer, and I would be curious to see another body system connected.
